summary: Client-abort storm causes runtime cleanup pile-up → threadpool saturation and API 5xx elevation
description:
Issue summary:
We observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses at the API gateway beginning ~2026-03-10 09:40 UTC for an affected dedicated tenant (BrightForms Inc.). Errors correlate with a large number of client-side stream cancellations/aborts (long-polling webhook flows).

Impact:
- ~12% 5xx error rate on tenant's streaming route over a 35m window, impacting live inference features for BrightForms (multiple customers report failures).
- Latency tail increased (p95→p99) and token throughput reduced for the tenant's dedicated pool.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC: Traffic spike starts from BrightForms long-poll clients (sustained connection churn and frequent client-initiated ABORTs).
- 09:40 UTC: API gateway begins returning 502/503s for streaming routes.
- 09:45 UTC: Alert fired (5xx rate > threshold).
- 09:50–10:10 UTC: Support engaged, routed to SRE and runtime team.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east dedicated pool for BrightForms.
- Serving runtime: release 1.18.2 (event-loop + blocking threadpool for model IO).
- API gateway: envoy proxy mesh with HTTP/2 streaming.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Client establishes long-lived HTTP/2 streaming session and issues prompt.
2) Client rapidly sends aborts/finishes (CANCEL frames) in tight loops (multiple concurrent sockets per client).
3) Runtime receives cancellations and schedules cleanup tasks that perform KV-cache unlocks, GIL-adjacent teardown, and metrics flushes on a shared blocking threadpool.
4) Threadpool becomes saturated; new request handoff to blocking workers is queued and stalls the runtime event loop, causing request timeouts and upstream 5xx to API gateway.

Observed behavior:
- High number of CANCEL frames recorded per second for the tenant.
- Worker thread pool depth near capacity; queue length grows.
- Runtime logs show extended cleanup task durations (10–20s) under the abort pattern.
- API gateway surfaces 502/503 to callers when upstream runtimes are slow or unresponsive.

Expected behavior:
- Graceful and fast cancellation handling without blocking the main request path; cancellations should be processed with bounded CPU and not occupy blocking threads for long periods.

Additional notes:
- This looks distinct from prior NVMe/gpu OOM/customer-prefetch issues; root cause appears tied to cancellation handling and cleanup semantics under high abort frequency.

comments: Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-10 09:48 UTC: Customer reports intermittent failures on live preview — errors start coinciding with a client rollout at 09:30. Asking for traffic window and sample client user-agent headers.

Customer (BrightForms) 2026-03-10 09:51 UTC: Sending logs and client patterns — new mobile SDK pushes a reconnect loop that cancels previous requests aggressively. Will provide SDK version and repro rate.

SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-03-10 10:01 UTC: Observed threadpool saturation for tenant. Hypothesis: cancellation handler performs heavy synchronous work on blocking threadpool. Recommending immediate mitigation: enable temporary rate-limit on concurrent streaming sessions for tenant and increase threadpool size to relieve backlog.

Runtime Eng (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10 10:12 UTC: Confirmed cleanup tasks include disk-backed metric flush and KV unlock which are blocking. Propose patch to offload metric flush to async queue and convert KV unlock to lock-free path. Will open a PR for safe rollout.

SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-03-11 03:00 UTC: Mitigation applied: tenant concurrent streaming cap reduced to 60 connections; threadpool temporary scaled +50%. 5xx rate reduced to baseline within 20 minutes.
investigation_notes: Correlation observed between client abort rate and blocking-pool queue length (Pearson r=0.82 over 30m window).
Heap and GPU stats show no memory fragmentation or driver resets; NVIDIA metrics within normal bounds for pool. Not a GPU OOM issue.
Tracing shows synchronous calls in cancellation path that touch disk (metric flush) and lock global kv-shard. These operations previously assumed low-frequency cancel events.
Prioritized repro harness created using a simulated SDK abort loop (100 clients, each issuing cancel 2–5s after request start). Reproduces blocking-pool queueing and upstream 502s within ~3 minutes.
Lock profiling indicates kv-shard lock hold time spikes to 12–18ms in the cancel path, multiplied by cancel rate causing pile-up.
workaround: Applied per-tenant concurrent streaming cap (60) and increased blocking threadpool capacity temporarily. Recommended customer to roll back mobile SDK aggressive reconnect until runtime patch is deployed.
resolution_plan: Short-term: merge PR to make metric flush asynchronous and relax KV lock scope (github.com/redwood/realtime-runtime/pull/412). Patch scheduled for canary 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC. Long-term: implement cancellable cleanup tokenization to bound work per cancellation and add server-side abort-rate circuit that sheds excessive aborting clients.
resolution_notes: Canary rollout started 2026-03-12 02:15 UTC; monitored tenant had 5xx drop from 12% → 1.8% within 10 minutes. No regressions observed in other tenants during canary. Full rollout planned 2026-03-12 08:00 UTC after 4h successful canary.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-1692: implement cancellation backpressure circuit (owner: Maya Chen)
OPS-881: add exporter metric for cancel-frame-rate per-tenant and alert on sustained >100 cancel/s (owner: Diego Morales)
DOCS-43: guidance for customers on safe reconnect/abort patterns in mobile SDK (owner: Developer Experience)
SEC-22: review that async metric flush does not expose PII in transit (owner: Security)
SRE-504: evaluate default threadpool sizing heuristic for dedicated pools under high abort-rate workloads
